rules.name: Direct Answer Definition Syntax
rules.description: Opening 40–60 words should state a direct, standalone definition or resolution formula to survive RAG chunking.
rules.remediation: Open with direct definition: '[Entity] is [category] designed to [outcome] by [mechanism]'.

rules.name: Passage Length Adaptive Chunking
rules.description: Key claim blocks should be self-contained within ~100–200 words (256–512 tokens).
rules.remediation: Split overly long passages (>250 words) into modular sub-sections with clear H2/H3 headers.

rules.name: Coreference Independence & Entity Naming
rules.description: Passage leads must name the entity directly rather than starting with ambiguous pronouns ('It', 'They', 'This tool').
rules.remediation: Replace ambiguous opening pronouns with explicit entity/protocol names.

rules.name: Empirical Verification & Metrics Density
rules.description: Claims should be backed by verified quantitative metrics with units or primary RFC/standard citations.
rules.remediation: Add verified benchmark metrics (e.g. latency ms, throughput, error rate) or primary RFC references.

rules.name: Zero Fabrication Integrity
rules.description: Content must contain zero fabricated credentials, quotes, or statistics; unverified data must use explicit placeholders.
rules.remediation: Replace unverified claims with verified telemetry or [VERIFY_BEFORE_PUBLISHING: URL] placeholders.

rules.name: Position-Adjusted Word Weighting (PAWC)
rules.description: Factual definitions, empirical metrics, and primary citations must be frontloaded in early positions and after headings to overcome exponential citation decay W = F * exp(-alpha * pos/N).
rules.remediation: Frontload key definitions and metrics in the first 60 words and immediately following H2/H3 headings.

rules.name: /llms.txt AI Context File & Syntax Compliance
rules.description: Site should publish a valid /llms.txt file containing an H1 title, blockquote summary, and structured documentation links for autonomous LLM agents.
rules.remediation: Create and publish /llms.txt at website root per Answer.AI specification (or run agy with --generate-llms-txt).

rules.name: AI Search Engine Retrieval Bot Permissibility
rules.description: Robots.txt should permit live search retrieval bots (OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot) to ensure visibility in AI answer engines.
rules.remediation: Allow search retrieval bots in robots.txt while maintaining training crawler restrictions if desired.

rules.name: Statistical Claims Outbound Source Grounding
rules.description: Numerical and statistical assertions should be accompanied by outbound anchor links to primary data sources, enabling AI retrieval crawlers to extract grounded citations.
rules.remediation: Add hyperlink citations (<a href='...'>) pointing directly to primary studies or RFC sources for numeric claims.

rules.name: Edge/WAF AI-Bot Accessibility Probe
rules.description: Edge WAF/Managed Challenge silently blocks AI crawlers despite robots.txt allowing them.

rules.name: CSR Fallback Content
rules.description: JS-heavy pages must carry noscript/SSR fallback for non-rendering AI crawlers.

rules.name: Citation Deep-Link Anchors
rules.description: Headings/tables need unique id anchors for fragment citations in AI answers.

rules.name: Inverted Pyramid per Section
rules.description: Each H2/H3 section should lead with a standalone claim in the first 40-60 words.

rules.name: Information Gain (Originality Signals)
rules.description: First-party results/benchmarks/formulas vs boilerplate water openers.

rules.name: llms-full.txt Full-Content Companion
rules.description: llms.txt companion dump for one-shot agent context loading.

rules.name: AI Slop Density (Citation-Killer Phrasing)
rules.description: Density of AI-slop phrasing (unsupported superlatives, hype verbs, corporate filler, hedging stacks, emoji-as-structure) per 1000 words. Generated-boilerplate register erodes the trust AI synthesis engines place in a passage.
rules.remediation: Replace unsupported superlatives with named facts (client, number, date). Flatten hedging stacks to one verifiable claim. Remove emoji used as document structure.

rules.name: Category-for-Audience Definition Pattern
rules.description: Opening block defines the entity as '[category] for [audience]' — the canonical self-description AI engines reuse verbatim when answering 'what is X / who is X for'.
rules.remediation: Open the page with one sentence of the form: '[Entity] is a [category] for [audience] that [outcome], proven by [evidence].'
